commands.name: create-dashboard-launch-token
commands.description:
Create Dashboard Launch Token
Mint a single-use launch URL for the dashboard.

Called by the launcher page right when readyz flips ready. The launch URL
is used as a top-level navigation; /launch then sets the oc_auth cookie
and 302s into the proxied dashboard.

The user's bearer token is stashed in Redis under the token's jti and
retrieved (atomic GETDEL) on /launch redeem — this keeps the bearer out of
the URL and out of any signed payload while preserving the existing proxy
auth flow (oc_auth cookie value = bearer token).

Refuses instances whose agent_type has has_dashboard=False (e.g. hermes).

options.name: --temperature
options.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic

options.name: --top-p
options.description: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

options.name: --min-p
options.description: Float that represents the minimum probability for a token to be considered, relative to the probability of the most likely token. Must be in [0, 1]. Set to 0 to disable this.

options.name: --top-k
options.description: Sample from the best k (number of) tokens. 0 means off

options.name: --max-tokens
options.description:
The maximum number of tokens to generate in the chat completion.
The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length. If explicitly set to None it will be the model's max context length minus input length or 65536, whichever is smaller.

options.name: --stop
options.description: up to 16 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens

options.name: --n

options.description: Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

options.name: --frequency-penalty
options.description: Positive values penalize new tokens based on how many times they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

options.name: --tools

options.name: --tool-choice
options.description: Controls which (if any) function is called by the model. none means the model will not call a function and instead generates a message. auto means the model can pick between generating a message or calling a function. required means the model must call a function. defined tool means the model must call that specific tool. none is the default when no functions are present. auto is the default if functions are present.

options.name: --repetition-penalty

options.name: --service-tier
options.description: The service tier used for processing the request. 'priority' processes the request with higher priority (premium rate); 'flex' processes it at lower priority for a discount, served only when spare capacity exists and may be retried/timed out under load. Both apply only to models that support the respective tier. For compatibility, 'auto' is treated as 'priority' and 'standard_only' as 'default'.

options.name: --fail-fast
options.description: If true, the request is rejected immediately with HTTP 429 when the model has no spare capacity, instead of waiting in the queue. Opt-in; the default (false) keeps standard queueing behavior. Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --models
options.description: Ordered list of up to 4 fallback models. The request is attempted on each model in order: when a model rejects it for lack of capacity (HTTP 429 model-busy / flex no-capacity), the next model is tried server-side. The first model that accepts serves the request; the response's model field and billing reflect that model, at that model's pricing. Models before the last are attempted without queueing (as if fail_fast were set); the last model honors the request's own fail_fast value. When models is set, the model field is ignored. Entries must be plain model names (no deploy_id:, custom_hostport, or :revision specifiers); duplicate entries are ignored, keeping the first occurrence.

options.name: --model
options.description: model name

options.name: --prompt
options.description: input prompt - a single string is currently supported

options.name: --max-tokens
options.description:
The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion.
The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length.If explicitly set to None it will be the model's max context length minus input length or 65536, whichever is smaller.

options.name: --temperature
options.description: What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic

options.name: --top-p
options.description: An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

options.name: --min-p
options.description: Float that represents the minimum probability for a token to be considered, relative to the probability of the most likely token. Must be in [0, 1]. Set to 0 to disable this.

options.name: --top-k
options.description: Sample from the best k (number of) tokens. 0 means off

options.name: --n
options.description: number of sequences to return

options.name: --stream
options.description: whether to stream the output via SSE or return the full response Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --logprobs
options.description: return top tokens and their log-probabilities

options.name: --echo
options.description: return prompt as part of the respons Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --stop
options.description: up to 16 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens

options.name: --presence-penalty
options.description: Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

options.name: --frequency-penalty
options.description: Positive values penalize new tokens based on how many times they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics.

options.name: --response-format
options.description: The format of the response. Currently, only json is supported.

options.name: --repetition-penalty
options.description: Alternative penalty for repetition, but multiplicative instead of additive (> 1 penalize, < 1 encourage)

options.name: --user
options.description: A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help  monitor and detect abuse. Avoid sending us any identifying information. We recommend hashing user identifiers.

options.name: --seed
options.description: Seed for random number generator. If not provided, a random seed is used. Determinism is not guaranteed.

options.name: --stop-token-ids
options.description: Up to 16 token IDs where the API will stop generating further tokens. Merged with the model's built-in stop tokens. Intended for private deployments.

options.name: --return-tokens-as-token-ids
options.description: return tokens as token ids Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --prompt-cache-key
options.description: A key to identify prompt cache for reuse across requests. If provided, the prompt will be cached and can be reused in subsequent requests with the same key.

options.name: --prompt-cache-options
options.description: Prompt cache options for this request's prefix, e.g. {"ttl": "1h"}.

options.name: --data
options.description: Optional multi-modal data to pass alongside the prompt. Only supported for a small number of non-chat-native vision models. Images must be base64 data URIs (e.g. 'data:image/png;base64,...').

options.name: --ignore-eos
options.description: Keep generating until max_tokens instead of stopping at the end-of-sequence token. Only honoured on models tagged with the allow_ignore_eos feature flag; ignored otherwise. Intended for benchmarking, where a fixed output length is needed. Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.
